## On-Call Handoff — Prod Outage 2026-07-04

**Status:** Resolved (service restarted by supervisor). Root cause needs follow-up fix — not yet patched.

### Impact Window
- **02:14:07 UTC** — first Redis error, degradation begins
- **02:31:52 UTC** — full service outage (api process group killed by supervisor)
- **Total degraded period:** ~17.5 minutes (elevated latency/timeouts) escalating to full outage in the last ~8 seconds
- Recovery: supervisor auto-restarted worker-2 at 02:31:45, but api was already unresponsive and got killed at 02:31:52. (Log ends there — confirm from deploy/infra tooling whether api came back up on its own or needed manual intervention.)

### Root Cause
Redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` became unreachable (`ECONNREFUSED`) at 02:14:07 and never recovered — 13 reconnect attempts (0–12) over the full window all failed against the same host/port.

App fell back to direct store reads on cache miss, which could not absorb the load: every read started timing out at 5000ms ("store overloaded"). Request queue depth grew unbounded — no backpressure or shedding was enforced once it passed its own configured max of 500 (climbed to 568+ with no rejection). The backlog held in memory until worker-2 hit `JavaScript heap out of memory`, crashed (exit 134), and the subsequent supervisor restart didn't recover fast enough before the api process group was killed as unresponsive.

**Contributing gaps:**
1. No circuit breaker on the store/DB path when Redis is down — kept retrying full-cost reads instead of failing fast.
2. Queue depth cap (500) was logged but not enforced — nothing rejected/shed work once exceeded.
3. No alerting surfaced on repeated Redis reconnect failures during the 17-minute window.

### ioredis Version
Could not confirm exact installed version — **no `package-lock.json` in repo**, only `package.json`, which pins a range: `"ioredis": "^5.4.1"` (allows any `5.x` ≥ 5.4.1, not exact).

Need to run `npm ls ioredis` on the actual prod host (or regenerate the lockfile) to get the resolved version before checking it against the changelog. Flagging this as a gap on its own — prod should have a committed lockfile for exactly this kind of incident forensics.

### Follow-ups
- [ ] Pin/commit `package-lock.json`; get exact `ioredis` version from prod, check changelog for reconnect-backoff fixes
- [ ] Enforce hard reject/shed at queue depth 500 (currently advisory only)
- [ ] Add circuit breaker around store reads when cache layer is degraded
- [ ] Alert on N consecutive Redis reconnect failures (don't wait for OOM to notice)
- [ ] Confirm why `10.0.0.12:6379` went down (infra/ops side)
